title: ある製品向けに書かれた仕様がAgent製品を跨ぐと成立せず、実装品質が製品依存で崩壊する
summary: Spec-driven開発で作成した仕様Artifactは、作成元のAgent製品に暗黙適合しており、別製品のAgentへ持ち込むと大幅な品質劣化を起こす。5製品(Kiro/Gemini/Copilot/Claude Code/Cursor)を跨いだ実測で、Kiro由来仕様をGeminiに投入した最悪ケースはToken F1 0.035、SQL構文妥当性2.33%まで落ちた。仕様のサイズ自体は実装品質を予測せず、仕様の書き直しは改善する一方、圧縮の効果は製品間で一貫しない。「仕様はVendor中立な資産」という前提が成り立たないことを示す。
proposed_category: 要求・仕様・正解定義

evidence.title: Specification Portability Across LLM Development Agents: Cross-Agent Compatibility in Specification-Driven Software Migration
evidence.summary: Two-stage study: 1,006 PL/SQL files (623 regenerated, 380 executed in PostgreSQL 16), then 1,802 Oracle scripts across five agents. Cross-agent transfer produces substantial agent-dependent degradation; specification size alone does not predict implementation quality; rewriting substantially improves performance while compression gives inconsistent benefits.

notes: Checked against H04 (agents interpret the same spec/interface differently) and K08 (session/skill formats fragmented per provider), D15 (skill owner/model/runtime unknown). H04 concerns concurrent divergent interpretation inside one project; K08 concerns session and skill format fragmentation, not spec-artifact fidelity. This is spec-artifact non-portability at handoff/migration time with a distinct response (renormalize or rewrite specs when switching agent products, and measure rather than assume transfer). Confidence held at medium because the study domain is narrow (Oracle-to-PostgreSQL SQL migration).
